desc:
A string is called smooth if it never has three equal letters in a row. Delete the fewest possible letters from s so that the result is smooth, and return the resulting string. The remaining letters keep their original order.

It can be shown that the result is unique.

"leeetcode"   -> "leetcode"
"aaabaaaa"    -> "aabaa"
"abc"         -> "abc"
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Only runs of identical letters can cause trouble. Think about what a single run of length L has to look like in the answer.
Deleting a letter from the middle of a run or from its end gives the same text, so which letters you delete does not matter, only how many are kept per run.
Scan left to right and append a letter to the answer unless the last two letters of the answer are already equal to it.
editorial: Two letters that are different never interact, so the problem decomposes into maximal runs of the same letter. A run of length L must be shortened to at most two letters, and cutting it to exactly min(L, 2) deletes the fewest letters. Removing letters never merges two different runs into one, because the neighbours of a run are different letters and that run keeps at least one letter.
Implementation: keep the answer in a list. For each character, check whether the last two entries both equal it; if so skip it, otherwise append. This is one pass over the string, O(n) time.
